what: The substitutions that show the instrument of Issue #405 measures what it claims to measure, and — after the fix — that each half of the fix is held by a check. Every run below was taken AFTER the state under test was committed, so reverting a mutant cannot revert the work with it.

howAMutantIsRun.substitution: sed -i "s/public const int CombatJoinSatiety = [0-9]*;/public const int CombatJoinSatiety = <value>;/" src/DungeonFortress.Simulation/PrototypeTuning.cs

mutantsOnTheInstrument.why: Criterion of the brief: «подстановка, меняющая порог входа, обязана сдвинуть измеренную долю в предсказанную сторону». An instrument that does not move with the number it is supposed to be measuring cannot be used to say whether that number is the cause.

M1.substitution: CombatJoinSatiety 30 -> 20, the value that stood before the balance slice. Nothing else changed.
M1.predicted: the share rises, starving refusals fall, and the four creatures the after-run names on the owner's seed come back into the line

measured.ownersSeedBaseline20260729: 97% (35/36), wave 3 back from 55% to 88% and wave 4 from 88% to 100%
measured.theNamedCreatures: #1 Кремень joins at t2080, #2 Мотылёк at t2080, #6 Прель at t2100, and #5 Уголёк joins wave 4 — the four the after-run reports as absent at satiety 25, 27, 26 and 22

M1.whatItProves: The instrument moves with the threshold, and the new absences on the owner's own party are the threshold's doing and not another part of the slice's. This is the substitution the attribution of Issue #405 rests on.

M2.predicted: hunger stops being able to keep anybody out at all

measured.note: combat_refused_starving disappears entirely and `thresholdSeen` goes empty

M2.whatItProves: Every starving refusal in the breakdown is the threshold's and nothing else's; there is no second door hunger keeps anybody out through.

M3.predicted: the share collapses and the floor check goes red

measured.suite: Most_of_the_domain_on_its_feet_takes_the_field RED — «Only 101 of 279 creature-slots on their feet took the field over 31 waves (36%), which is below the floor of 60%»

M3.whatItProves: The floor check is not vacuous: it is held by the admission threshold and it reddens when the threshold takes the line away. Without this the report could be green on a world where nobody musters at all.

mutantsOnTheFix.why: Rule 9 as narrowed by rule 21: the fix has two halves — the nearest-raider arm of contract 10.2 is added, and the larder arm is kept rather than traded for it — and a mutant must redden on each half separately, not on the change as a whole.
mutantsOnTheFix.theFix: PrototypeWorld.Combat.cs, DistanceToTheFight: the distance the admission rule compares against T.engage_radius is the smaller of the walk to LarderTiles[0] and the walk to the nearest raiding raider. Before it, only the larder walk was measured.

M4.half: the nearest-raider arm exists at all
M4.substitution: the call site goes back to the pre-fix line — `var distance = _map.Distance(creature.Position, PrototypeMap.LarderTiles[0], _zones[ZoneKind.Forbidden]);`
M4.predicted: A_creature_a_raider_is_already_near_is_not_turned_away_for_being_far_from_the_larder goes red and nothing else does
M4.measured: RED, exactly that check, 1 failed of 5. The other four including the larder-arm check stayed green.
M4.command: the python substitution above, then dotnet test tests/DungeonFortress.Simulation.Tests -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PrototypeMusterParticipationTests"; git checkout src/DungeonFortress.Simulation/PrototypeWorld.Combat.cs

M5.half: the larder arm is kept and not traded for the raider arm
M5.substitution: inside DistanceToTheFight, `var nearest = _map.Distance(... LarderTiles[0] ...)` and its early return are replaced by `int? nearest = null;`, leaving the raider arm alone
M5.measured: RED. It also reddens the raider-arm check, which is expected — this mutant breaks the distance rule on both sides — and the point stands because the larder-arm check is green under M4 and red only under M5.
M5.whatTheCheckCounts: 107 joins over the twelve parties that only the larder arm can account for: the creature was not mustering at the start of the tick, at least one raider stood on the map, and every one of them was further away in a straight line than the engage radius. All 107 are on `baseline`; on `prepared` the count is 0, because its creatures are already mustering when the wave lands and the muster escape carries them past the distance test.

mutantsOnTheFix.whyTheFirstAttemptAtM5IsRecordedToo: The larder-arm check was first written as «somebody joined while every raider was far away», and M5 left it green. The reason is a finding rather than a slip: the admission rule skips the distance test entirely for a creature that is mustering (`!creature.IsMustering`), so the check was being held by the muster escape and not by the larder arm. Requiring the joiner to have NOT been mustering, and requiring a raider to be on the map at all, is what made it measure the arm it names.

theCollateralOnIssue358.what: PrototypeReturningRaiderTests.A_returning_raider_walks_round_the_place_it_was_hit_hardest went red when the admission fix was applied, and repairing it is part of this branch.
theCollateralOnIssue358.howItWasDiagnosed: A throwaway probe walked every raider route of `baseline` over seeds 20260726..20260755 (30 parties) on two trees: the committed state of this branch with the fix stashed, and with it applied.
theCollateralOnIssue358.whatThatMeans: The check asserted the step outright, which is stronger than the mechanic it is about: RaiderStep walks round the remembered tile when there is a way round and straight through when there is not, and that fallback is what keeps avoidance from stranding anybody. The absolute claim was ALREADY false on the shipped world — it passed because it was pinned to RouteSeed = 20260729, one party on which it happened to hold. The admission fix moves the fight and 20260729 stops being that party.
theCollateralOnIssue358.theRepair: The check now reads the first twelve seeds of the same range and states what the mechanic promises: at most a fifth of the avoiders walk over their tile, and none is stranded. On those twelve parties the numbers are the same on both trees — 25 avoiders, 2 walked over, 0 stranded — so the repair is not a bar lowered to let this branch through. The stranding half is kept absolute, and it is the half the fix improves: 3 stranded on main over the full thirty, 0 with the fix.
theCollateralOnIssue358.whatWasNotDone: The mechanic of Issue #358 is not touched. Only the check that reads it is.
